correctness.rationale: The exchangeable face-mixture Dirichlet moments give a strictly positive scalar contrast covariance; the resulting symmetric reproducing kernel is explicitly 1+Gamma(sum t_i u_i-1/n). Convexity of its absolute row mass localizes the sharp essential supremum at vertices. A one-coordinate atom/Beta(1,s-1) mixture yields exactly 2B(1-nu)^s-1; the s=1 identity case is separate, and L1 equals Linfinity by symmetry/duality. Fixed-s and proportional-s limits follow by elementary expansions. The standalone standard-library checker passed 4563 assertions, including independent exact rational Gram inversions and beta polynomial integrals for all 3<=n<=11,1<=s<=n. Finite tests support but do not establish the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: Uniform sampling of simplicial lower-dimensional faces is a natural approximation design between vertex interpolation and full-volume least squares. The exact sharp norms for every genuine intermediate skeleton, their extremizing signs and two distinct dimension-asymptotic regimes are structurally informative and not implied by the two known endpoints. The face-balanced sampling model is explicit and reproducible, while the restriction to degree-one approximation is stated.
